name: Cathine

halfLifeEvidence.identity: the source is about this substance

effects: The second khat alkaloid — cathinone decays to cathine as the leaf dries, which is why khat is chewed fresh
Roughly an order of magnitude weaker than cathinone; mostly noradrenergic
Plasma half-life 5.2 ± 3.4 h after khat chewing — far longer than cathinone's 1.5 h
Formerly sold in Europe as an appetite suppressant (Exponcit, Adiposetten)
US Schedule IV and UN 1971 Schedule III; also a phenylpropanolamine stereoisomer, so it turns up in doping tests

mechanismOfAction.summary: Weak substrate-type releasing agent, NET > DAT. The reduced, β-hydroxy relative of cathinone.
mechanismOfAction.description: Cathine is (1S,2S)-2-amino-1-phenylpropan-1-ol: cathinone with the ketone reduced to an alcohol. That reduction costs most of the potency. Releasing activity is retained but roughly 7–10× weaker, and skewed toward noradrenaline over dopamine, giving a peripheral sympathomimetic and anorectic profile rather than a euphoriant one. Its much longer half-life is why khat's tail outlasts its peak.
